## Results
The data is unambiguous and surprising. Let me analyze it.

**Key findings from the data:**

The storage metrics directly **refute** storage being the bottleneck. The file system is essentially idle for data I/O across the entire 10-day window, except for two brief activity spikes.

**1. FreeDataStorageCapacity — the file system is nearly empty, not filling up:**
- Baseline (Sep 21–23): 1,174,307,209,216 bytes free (~1.094 TiB) — flat
- Recent (Sep 25 – Oct 1): 1,165,707,706,368 bytes free (~1.086 TiB) — flat
- Total provisioned ≈ 1.17 TiB. **StorageCapacityUtilization is only ~1.85% → 2.56%** across the whole window. The file system is **~97% empty**. It is NOT filling up, so the SCRATCH_2 "degrades as it fills" mechanism does not apply here. Free capacity dropped by only ~8.6 GB over 10 days.

**2. DataReadBytes / DataWriteBytes — virtually zero read throughput:**
- On almost every 6h bucket, DataReadBytes ≈ 131–143 KB (i.e. ~0.006 KB/s — effectively noise, no real reads).
- The only two reads of substance: Sep 24 00:00 (19.85 GB in 6h ≈ **0.92 MB/s**) and Sep 24 18:00 (71.0 GB in 6h ≈ **3.29 MB/s**). These are tiny.
- Recent days (Sep 28 – Oct 1): DataReadBytes stays at ~131 KB per 6h ≈ **0.006 KB/s**. There is essentially **no dataset reading happening from this FSx file system in the recent window.**

**3. Effective read throughput — nowhere near the ~234 MB/s ceiling:**
- Peak observed read throughput over the entire 10 days: ~3.3 MB/s (Sep 24). That is **~1.4% of the 234 MB/s SCRATCH_2 ceiling.** No saturation whatsoever.

**4. FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization / NetworkThroughputUtilization:**
- Disk throughput utilization: baseline ~0.05–0.14%, peaks of 7.2% / 5.7% during the two Sep 24 and Sep 29 activity bursts. Normal recent values ~0.05–0.13%. **Disk is nearly idle.**
- Network throughput utilization: ~0.005–0.047% baseline, with two spikes to 97% and 124.7% on Sep 24 (the data load events). Recent days back to ~0.005–0.047%. **No sustained network pressure.**

**5. IOPS / Metadata:**
- DataReadOperations: steady ~32–33 ops per 6h (baseline AND recent) — flat, trivial. Two spikes on Sep 24 (129,506 and 178,390 ops) during the loads.
- MetadataOperations: steady ~1,120–1,170 per 6h (baseline AND recent). Two spikes on Sep 24 (~204k and ~200k). **No recent metadata bottleneck or trend.**

**Interpretation of the two Sep 24 spikes:** These look like a one-time dataset ingest/load (large writes + reads + heavy metadata, saturating network briefly). ## Findings

**Verdict: Storage is NOT the bottleneck. The FSx for Lustre file system metrics firmly REFUTE the storage hypothesis.** (Respond entirely in English, per directive.)

**Resource:** FSx for Lustre `fs-077c776983688ad76` (arn:aws:fsx:us-west-2:111122223333:file-system/fs-077c776983688ad76), SCRATCH_2, ~1.17 TiB provisioned, SCRATCH_2 baseline ceiling ≈ 234 MB/s.
**Window analyzed:** 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z → 2026-10-01T04:08:00Z, 6h period.

### 1. The file system is nearly empty — the "fills up → throughput degrades" mechanism does NOT apply
- `StorageCapacityUtilization`: **1.85% (baseline Sep 21–23) → 2.56% (recent Sep 25–Oct 1).** The file system is ~97% empty throughout.
- `FreeDataStorageCapacity`: 1,174,307,209,216 bytes (~1.094 TiB free, baseline) → 1,165,707,706,368 bytes (~1.086 TiB free, recent). Net drop ≈ 8.6 GB over 10 days — flat, no fill-up trend.
- Because the file system is nowhere near full, SCRATCH_2 disk-throughput degradation from low `FreeDataStorageCapacity` is not occurring. **Noteworthy criterion #1 (fill-up correlated with throughput decline) is NOT met.**

### 2. Read throughput is effectively zero — far below the 234 MB/s ceiling, no saturation
- `DataReadBytes` sits at ~131–143 KB per 6h bucket for nearly every period (≈ **0.006 KB/s** — noise, not real dataset reads), including every recent bucket Sep 28 → Oct 1.
- Peak read throughput over the entire 10 days was only ~3.3 MB/s (Sep 24 18:00, 71.0 GB/6h). That is **~1.4% of the 234 MB/s SCRATCH_2 ceiling.** No capping, no saturation (criterion #2 NOT met).
- `DataReadOperations`: flat ~32–33 ops/6h in both baseline and recent windows (trivial).

### 3. No step-change aligning with the "last few days" slowdown
- Only two activity events, both on **Sep 24**: 00:00 (read 19.85 GB ≈ 0.92 MB/s, write 22.8 GB, 129.5k read-ops, 204k metadata-ops, network util 97%) and 18:00 (read 71.0 GB ≈ 3.29 MB/s, write 71.7 GB, 178.4k read-ops, 200k metadata-ops, network util 124.7%, disk util 7.2%). These look like a one-time dataset ingest/load, after which the FS returned to idle.
- Recent days (Sep 28 – Oct 1) show the SAME idle baseline as Sep 21–23. There is **no inflection point in any FSx metric in the recent window** (criterion #3 NOT met).

### 4. No metadata bottleneck
- `MetadataOperations`: flat ~1,120–1,170 per 6h in both baseline and recent windows; the only spikes (~200k) were the Sep 24 load events. No recent small-file/metadata pressure (criterion #4 NOT met).

### Utilization sanity checks (file server OSS0000)
- `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization`: ~0.05–0.14% nominal, peaks 7.2%/5.7% only during Sep 24/29 bursts — disk nearly idle.
- `NetworkThroughputUtilization`: ~0.005–0.047% nominal, 97%/124.7% only during the two Sep 24 loads — no sustained pressure.

**From Sep 24 20:00 onward through Sep 27 11:00 (termination):** both nodes drop to ~2.6–3.3 MB/hour (≈ **6 Kbps**) — essentially idle, with tiny periodic ~26 MB/h spikes (hourly cron/heartbeat chatter). No high-throughput training ever resumed.

## FINDINGS — p6-b200 Throughput Triage (account 111122223333, us-west-2)

### PART A — GPU metrics availability: **NONE published to CloudWatch (investigation gap)**

I enumerated every custom namespace in the account/region. **No DCGM, NVIDIA, nvidia_gpu, or any GPU-telemetry namespace exists for the ParallelCluster fleet.** Confirmed by two independent paths:

- **CloudWatch `list_metrics`**: The only custom namespaces are `CWAgent`, `ParallelCluster`, `FsxTrainingObservability`, `AWS/Prometheus`, and `/aws/sagemaker/Clusters`. None carry DCGM-style GPU metrics for the p6-b200 nodes:
  - `CWAgent` → only `mem_used_percent`, `disk_used_percent` (dims: InstanceId, path/device/fstype). **No GPU metrics.**
  - `ParallelCluster` → only `ClustermgtdHeartbeat` (dims: InstanceId, ClusterName).
  - `FsxTrainingObservability` → only mem/disk.
  - `AWS/Prometheus` → only AMP workspace operational metrics (RuleEvaluations, QuerySamplesProcessed, etc.) — **no DCGM series ingested**.
  - `/aws/sagemaker/Clusters` → has `node_gpu_utilization`, `node_gpu_memory_*` etc. but dimensioned by **`ClusterId`** (SageMaker HyperPod), **NOT** the ParallelCluster InstanceId fleet. Different workload — out of scope.
- **CloudWatch PromQL surface** (`list_prometheus_metadata`): no metric matching `DCGM.*` and no metric matching `.*gpu.*` is queryable. 

**Conclusion for Part A:** None of DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL, DCGM_FI_DEV_SM_CLOCK, DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP, DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE, DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS, DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS, ECC, or NVLink metrics are available in CloudWatch for this fleet. **GPU health cannot be assessed from CloudWatch.** This is an explicit investigation gap — the DCGM/dcgm-exporter → CloudWatch (or → AMP) pipeline was not configured on this cluster.

### PART B — Instance identification & network/EC2 metrics

**Identified 2 p6-b200 nodes** by cross-referencing EC2 NetworkIn across all InstanceId dimensions (describe_instances returns empty — instances already terminated; metrics retained):

# Findings: ParallelCluster CloudWatch Logs — `distributed-training-triage-b200`

## Log group identified
`/aws/parallelcluster/distributed-training-triage-b200-202608261551` (account 111122223333, us-west-2). Window searched: Sep 18 → Oct 1 2026 (focused Sep 23–27, which is where all recent GPU-node activity lives).

## ⚠️ Critical data-availability caveat
The HeadNode daemon streams that normally hold scaling decisions — **`clustermgtd`, `clustermgtd_events`, `slurmctld`, `slurm_resume`, `slurm_suspend`** (HeadNode `i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8`) — **stopped ingesting to CloudWatch in April 2026** (last event `1788186580` ≈ 2026-04-29). There are **no `slurm_resume`/`slurm_suspend` streams at all** in the recent window. All recent evidence therefore comes from the **compute-node** streams (`computemgtd`, `slurmd`, `system-messages`, `slurm_health_check`). Scaling API errors (InsufficientCapacity, etc.) would be in `slurm_resume`/`clustermgtd` — **not retrievable from logs**; this must be confirmed via CloudTrail/EC2 by another agent.

## Cluster configuration (recovered verbatim from `cloud-init-output`)
This is the single most important finding and reframes the whole investigation:
- `'CapacityType': 'CAPACITY_BLOCK'`
- `'CapacityReservationTarget': {'CapacityReservationId': 'cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b'}`
- `'InstanceType': 'p6-b200.48xlarge'`, `'MinCount': 2, 'MaxCount': 2`, `'Name': 'p6b20048xlarge'`
- `'ScalingStrategy': 'all-or-nothing'`, `'ScaledownIdletime': 10`

➡️ The GPU fleet is **2 STATIC nodes** (Min=Max=2), **not dynamically Slurm-scaled**, and is backed by a **Capacity Block** (`cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b`). Static Capacity-Block nodes exist only for the life of the reservation.

## Timeline (ordered by timestamp, UTC)

| Time | Event (verbatim where quoted) |
|---|---|
| **Sep 23 11:30–11:33** | Boot of first GPU pair `i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807` (10.0.33.57) + `i-0190035035290b380` (10.0.45.214). Clean EFA/NVIDIA init. `"slurmd version 25.11.6 started"`, `CPUs=192 ... Memory=2043929`. |
| Sep 23 15:51:45 | First pair stops ingesting (`i-0a3c…`, `i-0190…` last event). |
| Sep 23 16:03–16:12 | Short-lived pair `i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb` (10.0.33.215) + `i-0ce092c23d7562556` (10.0.33.211) boot and stop (~9 min). |
| **Sep 23 16:19–16:22** | Final/long-lived GPU pair boots: `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f` (10.0.38.160, `gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-2`) + `i-0be6193831c898671` (10.0.38.23, `gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1`). |

| **Sep 24 02:32–19:29** | Dense multi-node training (JobIds 31–69) across BOTH nodes (10.0.38.23 + 10.0.38.160). | **Sep 27 10:59:54** | **All compute streams stop simultaneously** on both `i-0014…` and `i-0be6…`. Clean cutoff — no shutdown target, no power-off, no DRAIN/DOWN, no error, no GPU/EFA fault preceding it. Fleet → 0. |

## Node count per day (p6-b200 compute nodes seen in logs)
- **Sep 18–22:** 0 nodes (no streams).
- **Sep 23:** up to 2 concurrent, with churn (3 pairs cycled; final stable pair up from 16:22).
- **Sep 24:** 2 nodes, active multi-node training all day until 19:29.
- **Sep 25–26:** 2 nodes UP but idle (heartbeat only, no jobs).
- **Sep 27:** 2 nodes until **10:59:54**, then **0**.
- **Sep 28 – Oct 1:** 0 nodes.

## What the logs reveal about the four hypotheses

**1. GPU health — RULED OUT.** No `Xid`, no `"fallen off the bus"`, no `Uncorrectable`/ECC errors, no NVLink down, no row-remap, no PCIe AER, no `RmInitAdapter failed`. A distill of all 9,679 keyword matches confirmed they are **100% benign boot-time noise** (`"loading NVIDIA UNIX Open Kernel Module"`, `"kbifCacheVFInfo_GB100: Unable to read NV_PF0_INITIAL_AND_TOTAL_VFS"`). The one ParallelCluster GPU health check that ran **passed with exit code 0**. Nodes were never set DRAIN/DOWN for health.

**2. EFA / network — RULED OUT (as a hardware fault).** EFA v3.1.0g loaded cleanly on every boot, all `efa_N: IB device registered`. No `libfabric`/`ibv_`/RDMA errors, no NCCL timeouts in logs. (Note: NCCL/training stdout is **not** shipped to CloudWatch — it goes to `/fsx` output files — so NCCL-level throughput cannot be confirmed here, but no network *faults* surfaced in system logs.)

**3. Capacity — THE LEADING EXPLANATION.** The fleet is **static nodes on Capacity Block `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b`**. The nodes did not "shrink due to a fault": they ran healthy (valid clustermgtd heartbeat to the final second) and then **both terminated simultaneously and cleanly at Sep 27 10:59:54** with no OS shutdown sequence and no error — the classic signature of a **Capacity Block reservation reaching its end time** (EC2 reclaims the instances). The repeated Sep 23 node churn (3 pairs in ~5 hours) is also consistent with Capacity-Block / all-or-nothing provisioning behavior.

**4. Throughput degradation.** No throughput numbers (samples/sec, tokens/sec, step time) exist in CloudWatch — training output is on FSx. What logs DO show is that from Sep 24 02:32 onward, nearly every training step was **CANCELLED by SIGNAL Killed** (`step_rc: 9`, SIGABRT `134`) rather than completing — i.e., the multi-node jobs were repeatedly dying/being killed. Active training effectively **ended Sep 24 19:29**; the nodes then sat idle for ~2.6 days before the Capacity Block ended on Sep 27.

## Bottom line
- **Not GPUs, not network hardware.** Zero GPU faults (no Xid/ECC/NVLink) and zero EFA/RDMA faults in any node log; the GPU health check passed.
- **The GPU fleet shrank to zero because the Capacity Block reservation `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b` ended** — both static p6-b200.48xlarge nodes were reclaimed cleanly and simultaneously at **2026-09-27 10:59:54 UTC**, with the HeadNode controller healthy right up to that instant. Active training had already stopped at **Sep 24 19:29** (jobs repeatedly killed, then 2+ idle days).
- The "throughput drop over the last few days" aligns with: usable compute present only Sep 23–24, degrading job completions (steps killed) on Sep 24, then **no GPU capacity at all after Sep 27 10:59**.

## Recommended follow-ups (outside log scope)
1. **Confirm Capacity Block `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b` end time** via EC2 `describe_capacity_block_offerings`/`describe_capacity_reservations` and CloudTrail (another agent) — this is the decisive check.
2. The HeadNode CloudWatch agent for `clustermgtd`/`slurmctld`/`slurm_resume` has not shipped logs since **April 2026** — scaling/launch failures (InsufficientCapacity, bootstrap errors) could not be examined; verify via CloudTrail `RunInstances`/`CreateFleet` errors for subnet `subnet-024dbe437aef9d7eb`.
3. The repeated `SIGNAL Killed`/`step_rc: 9/134` job terminations on Sep 24 are worth examining in the FSx `/fsx` training output files (not in CloudWatch) to see if the throughput complaint predates the capacity loss.

{"id": "7334b1e5-9dd1-402d-b32a-3bdcccded5d8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"thinking": "With three strong results now in hand, I'm pulling everything together into a timeline and classification. The capacity block lifecycle findings show block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is a p6-b200.48xlarge with 2 nodes in us-west-2d, purchased Sep 22 at 19:28 with an original window running Sep 23 11:30 through Sep 25.

The extension purchased Sep 24 at 02:35 pushed the end date to Sep 27 at 11:30 UTC, but the reservation expired on schedule and was purged -- every RunInstances call now fails because the capacity reservation is no longer active. There's a replacement block, cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, but it's the wrong instance type (p6-b300) and wrong AZ (us-west-2b), so it doesn't satisfy the launch template, which still references the dead reservation.

Looking at the ParallelCluster logs, the fleet consisted of 2 static CAPACITY_BLOCK nodes pinned to that same block, which terminated cleanly and simultaneously right at Sep 27 10:59:54 UTC, just before the block's end time. There were no GPU, EFA, or NCCL faults -- health checks all passed -- but active training that ran Sep 24 02:32-19:29 shows many steps cancelled.

Checking the GPU and network metrics, I notice there's no GPU telemetry (DCGM/nvidia) shipped to CloudWatch, which limits visibility into GPU health through metrics alone, though the system logs already ruled out hardware faults. Network throughput looked healthy though -- EFA hit 121-631 Gbps during the Sep 24 training burst, with no degradation. The fleet was active from Sep 23 16:00 to roughly Sep 27 11:00, but high-throughput activity only occurred on Sep 24, with nodes sitting idle afterward until termination.

Now I'm piecing together the master timeline: the Capacity Block was purchased Sep 22 at 19:28 for two p6-b200.48xlarge instances in us-west-2d, valid from Sep 23 11:30 to Sep 25 11:30. The block started Sep 23 11:30 with the first GPU pair launching, though there was churn with three pairs cycling through that day before a stable pair booted at 16:19-16:22 and passed GPU health checks. Dense multi-node training ran Sep 24 from 02:32 to 19:29 with healthy EFA throughput, but many steps were cancelled by SIGABRT signals.

An extension to the Capacity Block was purchased at 02:35 on Sep 24, pushing the end date to Sep 27 11:30. Training activity stopped at 19:29 that day, and the nodes sat idle but healthy through Sep 25-26 with no jobs running. At 10:59:54 on Sep 27, both nodes terminated simultaneously as the Capacity Block ended, dropping the fleet to zero. From 11:05-11:19, the head node repeatedly tried and failed to launch new instances because the capacity reservation was no longer active, and by 11:30 the block's scheduled end date hit, releasing the reservation entirely. The fleet stayed pinned at zero from 11:30 through October 1st, with every scale-up attempt failing, until a replacement Capacity Block for p6-b300 instances in us-west-2b became active on Sep 30 at 11:30.

I'm now identifying this as the root cause: the p6-b200 Capacity Block expired at its scheduled end time, the ParallelCluster fleet requires both static nodes tied to that specific reservation, and since the launch template still references the dead reservation ID, every node launch attempt fails outright. This explains the zero training throughput over the past several days, and the fix is clear — purchase a new p6-b200 Capacity Block and update the launch template to point to the new reservation ID. # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### B200 training throughput drop reading from FSx Lustre
**Description:** Distributed-training throughput for the B200 GPU cluster reading from FSx for Lustre file system fs-077c776983688ad76 has degraded noticeably over the last few days (~Sept 27 – Oct 1 2026). Root cause (storage/network/GPU) not yet determined.
**Time:** 2026-09-27T00:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: GPU compute fleet capacity reservation not found
**Description:** The b200 compute fleet's launch template (lt-025a88cbeaba7b869, instance type p6-b200.48xlarge, subnet subnet-024dbe437aef9d7eb, same subnet as the FSx file system, 8 EFA-only interfaces) targets a capacity block reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b via CapacityReservationSpecification. DescribeCapacityReservations returns InvalidCapacityReservationId.NotFound for this ID — the reservation the fleet depends on to launch GPU instances no longer exists. No p6-b200 (or any GPU-family) instances are running, stopped, or terminated anywhere in the account/region, and no RunInstances events for this instance type appear in CloudTrail for the investigation window. This could prevent the Slurm compute fleet from scaling up, which would show up as degraded distributed-training throughput.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-throughput-drop

#### Gaps
- **B200 GPU compute fleet could not be located:** No GPU instances (p6-b200, p5/p5e/p5en, p4d/p4de families) were found running, stopped, or terminated anywhere in account 111122223333 / us-west-2, nor in the FSx subnet subnet-024dbe437aef9d7eb or VPC vpc-0028c20959269e96f. Only two ParallelCluster t3.medium HeadNodes exist (for clusters 'distributed-training-triage' and 'distributed-training-triage-b200'). The GPU compute nodes are likely a Slurm dynamic fleet currently scaled to zero, but this means direct GPU-side metrics (utilization, NVLink, etc.) are not yet available to rule GPUs in or out as the bottleneck.

### Root Cause: Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b expired, blocking GPU node relaunch
**Description:** CloudTrail shows the ParallelCluster head node (i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8) repeatedly failing RunInstances for the p6-b200.48xlarge static compute nodes starting ~2026-09-27T11:13Z, with error 'Client.InvalidParameterValue: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active.' This lines up exactly with the Capacity Block's extended end time (2026-09-27T11:30Z — originally purchased 2026-09-22T19:28Z for 2026-09-23T11:30Z→2026-09-25T11:30Z, extended +48h on 2026-09-24T02:35Z to end 2026-09-27T11:30Z). The cluster's compute fleet is configured as CAPACITY_BLOCK-backed STATIC nodes (MinCount=MaxCount=2, ScalingStrategy=all-or-nothing), so once the block expired, ParallelCluster could not relaunch the 2 GPU nodes at all — training throughput did not merely degrade, it dropped to zero GPU compute after 2026-09-27T11:30Z. This is the fundamental cause: fixing it (renewing/replacing the capacity reservation) is what would restore training.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-throughput-drop

#### Gaps
- **Why the Capacity Block reservation disappeared is unknown:** It is not yet established whether cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b expired naturally (Capacity Blocks have a fixed duration/end date), was manually cancelled/released, or was never valid for this launch template version. Need to check the Capacity Block's end date/history and ParallelCluster compute-fleet / Slurm logs for launch failure errors to confirm.
- **No GPU/DCGM telemetry published to CloudWatch:** Enumerated every CloudWatch namespace in the account; none carry DCGM/NVIDIA GPU metrics (utilization, SM clock, temperature, XID/ECC, NVLink) for the ParallelCluster p6-b200 fleet. CWAgent only publishes mem/disk; the SageMaker /aws/sagemaker/Clusters GPU metrics belong to an unrelated HyperPod workload. This means GPU hardware degradation during the Sep 24 training window could not be confirmed or ruled out from CloudWatch alone (log-based evidence of no Xid/ECC faults was used instead as a secondary signal).

## Other Gaps

### Cannot confirm cause of Sep 24 training step kills
**Description:** The repeated SIGKILL/SIGABRT terminations of training steps on Sep 24 could not be explained because NCCL logs and application-level throughput metrics are written to FSx /fsx output files, which were not accessible to the CloudWatch/CloudTrail-based tooling used in this investigation. Recommend the cluster owner inspect the /fsx training output/log files directly.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore GPU capacity to AWS ParallelCluster "distributed-training-triage-b200" by purchasing a new p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block in us-west-2d (usw2-az4) sized for 2 nodes, then repointing compute launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 and the ParallelCluster configuration from the expired reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b to the new reservation ID.

## Reasoning
The Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b (2x p6-b200.48xlarge, usw2-az4) expired 2026-09-27 11:30 UTC and was purged. The launch template still pins the dead reservation ID, so every RunInstances for the 2 static all-or-nothing GPU nodes fails with 'Capacity Reservation ... is not active', leaving the fleet at zero since Sep 27. The already-active replacement block cr-0580a9d7420fd589a is the wrong type (p6-b300) and AZ (us-west-2b) with only 1 instance, so it cannot be reused. At planning time the only purchasable p6-b200 offering was in us-west-2a, not the required usw2-az4 — this gates the purchase step on an AZ match, with cross-AZ fallback documented as a temporary-only option. FSx storage, EFA networking, and GPU hardware were all ruled out as healthy.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

```
aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --versions '$Latest' '$Default' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Capture the current launch template configuration (version 4, pinned to the dead reservation) as the rollback baseline.
**Advisory:** Version 4 still references the dead reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b, so this baseline is a reference point only, not a healthy state to return to.

#### 1.2 Capture the current ParallelCluster CloudFormation stack parameters and…

**Purpose:** Capture the current ParallelCluster CloudFormation stack parameters and status as a rollback baseline.

#### 1.3 Record the current cluster status (zero GPU nodes) and retrieve the…

```
pcluster describe-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --region us-west-2 && pcluster describe-cluster-instances --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Record the current cluster status (zero GPU nodes) and retrieve the cluster configuration YAML as the baseline for the config edit.
**Advisory:** Run from an environment with ParallelCluster CLI v3.16.0 configured for account 111122223333.


#### 2.2 Find a p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block offering in usw2-az4 matching…

```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-block-offerings --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-count 2 --capacity-duration-hours 24 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Find a p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block offering in usw2-az4 matching the pinned compute subnet and FSx AZ; retry with other durations (48/72/168h) if none is listed.
**Risks:** At planning time only a us-west-2a (usw2-az1) offering was available, not usw2-az4; do not purchase an offering in the wrong AZ against the existing usw2-az4 subnet, since instances cannot launch outside their subnet's AZ.
**Advisory:** If only a non-usw2-az4 offering is available, treat a cross-AZ fallback as temporary only — it adds cross-AZ latency/cost versus FSx fs-077c776983688ad76 in us-west-2d.

**Purpose:** Acquire a new p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block in usw2-az4 sized for 2 nodes to restore GPU capacity.

**Risks:** May require stopping/restarting the compute fleet; the HeadNode stays up throughout. No training is currently running (fleet is at zero), so no active job is interrupted.

```
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:parallelcluster:cluster-name,Values=distributed-training-triage-b200 Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running --region us-west-2 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,Type:InstanceType,State:State.Name,AZ:Placement.AvailabilityZone}'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the 2 static GPU nodes launch and reach running state in us-west-2d alongside the HeadNode.
**Advisory:** Also confirm Slurm node registration (sinfo/scontrol show nodes) and that training throughput resumes.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Revert the launch template default version to the pre-change version 4…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --default-version 4 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Revert the launch template default version to the pre-change version 4 if the new reservation proves faulty.
**Risks:** Version 4 still references the dead reservation and cannot launch instances on its own — this only reverts the change, it does not restore a working fleet.
**Advisory:** If a cluster config update was applied, also roll it back by re-running pcluster update-cluster with the configuration YAML captured during prepare.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Eliminate the stale Capacity Block reference and single-AZ/single-reservation fragility in the cluster's infrastructure definition.
**Description:** Parameterize CapacityReservationId in the cluster configuration / IaC that renders launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 instead of hard-coding it, and add operational guardrails around Capacity Block lifecycle.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Cluster configuration no longer hard-codes cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b; the reservation ID is a parameter.
- A documented runbook/automation acquires a replacement p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block in usw2-az4 and repoints the cluster before the current reservation's EndDate.
- An alarm or scheduled check warns ahead of Capacity Block expiry and/or when the GPU fleet is at zero running nodes while jobs are queued.
- Compute subnet AZ and targeted Capacity Block AZ are validated to match (usw2-az4), staying co-located with FSx fs-077c776983688ad76.
